contributions.headingText: Primary cutaneous CD8-positive aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma (PCAETL) is a neoplastic proliferation of T lymphocytes often expressing CD8 along with cytotoxic molecules, characterized by epidermal necrosis, a high proliferation index, and aggressive clinical behaviour.
9709/3 Primary cutaneous CD8-positive aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma

2B0Y & XH2513 Other specified primary cutaneous mature T-cell or NK-cell lymphomas and lymphoproliferative disorders & Primary cutaneous CD8-positive aggressive epidermotropic cytotoxic T-cell lymphoma
Not recommended: Berti lymphoma; Ketron–Goodman / disseminated pagetoid reticulosis.
Patients present with generalized or localized skin lesions. The oral mucosa may be involved {28128277; 35001425}.

PCAETL is characterized by localized or (more commonly) diffusely distributed papules, ulcerated nodules, tumours, and plaques, showing erosion or central necrosis {10433941; 24438036; 28128277}. In some patients these lesions may be preceded by chronic poorly defined patches {28128277}. PCAETL may disseminate to visceral sites (lung, testes, CNS); lymph nodes are usually spared {28128277}. Typically, PCAETL is not associated with immunosuppression.
PCAETL is rare, accounting for < 1% of all cutaneous T-cell lymphomas. It occurs in adults and has a male predilection {10433941; 30635287; 24438036; 28128277}.

Genomic events that recurrently impact genes with roles in the cell cycle, chromatin regulation, and the JAK/STAT pathway have been described in PCAETL, including complex genomic rearrangements and various JAK2 fusions {33792220}. Upregulated JAK-2 signalling is observed in virtually all cases, whereas this feature is not detected in other cytotoxic cutaneous T-cell lymphomas. In fusion-negative cases, gain-of-function mutations in JAK2, STAT3, and STAT5B, and loss of negative regulators of the JAK/STAT pathway, particularly SH2B3, can be observed {33792220}.
PCAETL appears as roundish lesions showing erosive or ulcerative features (see Clinical features).

Although the infiltrate can involve the entire dermis, pagetoid epithelial involvement (epidermal and adnexal) is typically observed {24438036; 28391645}. Spongiosis can lead to blister formation. The dermal infiltrates are monomorphic to pleomorphic. Rimming of subcutaneous fat spaces has been reported {22226429}. Tumour cells are usually atypical small to large lymphocytes with indented nuclei, scant cytoplasm, and occasional immunoblastic features {10433941; 28128277}. Histological evidence of cytotoxicity, including epidermal necrosis/ulceration, dermal necrosis, karyorrhexis, and rare angiocentric destruction, is present {10433941; 22226429; 24438036; 28128277}. Ulceration may mimic pyoderma gangrenosum {19438529; 30259963}. Atypical CD8+ cytotoxic T cells show striking pagetoid epidermotropism {15692063; 10433941; 24438036; 28128277}, especially in cases with diffuse lesions. The clinicopathological features are summarized in #29994Table 5.11 {24438036; 22226429}.

Immunohistochemistry

The usual markers are listed in #29994Table 5.11 . Immunohistochemistry for phosphorylated STAT3 and phosphorylated STAT5 can also be used to detect activation of the JAK/STAT pathway {30307677; 33792220; 34432866}.

Differential diagnosis

This includes rare epidermotropic subtypes of cutaneous gamma-delta T-cell lymphomas (e.g. gamma-delta mycosis fungoides), CD8+ mycosis fungoides, localized pagetoid reticulosis, and type D lymphomatoid papulosis (#36203Table 5.12).
The use of FNAB is not recommended for the diagnosis of this entity.
Evidence of clonal TR gene rearrangements supports the diagnosis.

Essential: an epidermotropic and adnexotropic cutaneous diffuse infiltrate composed of pleomorphic cytotoxic TCRαβ-expressing T lymphocytes; ulcerated or erosive plaques and tumours without spontaneous resolution.

Desirable: demonstration of activating mutations or fusions of JAK-2 pathway genes.
PCAETL is staged according to the TNM classification system for cutaneous T-cell lymphomas other than mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome {17540844}.
PCAETL have an aggressive course (median survival time: 12 months). There are no differences between cases with small or large cell morphology or localized or diffuse lesions {28128277}.
